findings.description: Every RateLimitError above the probed bound terminates the invocation, including ordinary request-rate throttling.
findings.failure_mode: With the derived policy enabled, an RPM 429 returns RATE_LIMITED without trying the declared fallback chain, even though the error says nothing about payload size. The supplied test_request_rate_429_while_unverified_walks_to_the_next_hop exercises this regression.
findings.suggested_fix: Require the error's token-limit classification before taking the calibration exit; preserve normal fallback behavior for request-rate throttling.

findings.description: _ceiling_unverified is calculated for the head entry and reused for every fallback entry.
findings.failure_mode: After an unverified head fails for a walkable reason, a calibrated fallback's context rejection is incorrectly classified as CEILING_UNVERIFIED_LIMIT. Its rate-limit errors also incorrectly take the non-walkable calibration path. Conversely, an unverified fallback reached from a verified head misses that handling.
findings.suggested_fix: Calculate unverified status for each dispatched hop using that entry's calibration, probed bound, and applicable input count; use this local value in both exception handlers.

findings.description: The long-context threshold excludes cache-read and cache-creation input tokens.
findings.failure_mode: For example, 50K uncached input plus 200K cached input exceeds the 200K prompt threshold, but input_tokens alone does not. The ledger records base rates for the entire request and omits long_context, understating spend and weakening budget enforcement. The ledger explicitly documents cache tokens as separate from input_tokens.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare the threshold against input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_creation_tokens, while continuing to price each category at its corresponding rate.

findings.description: The context-shrink branch continues the existing bounded retry loop even when its final iteration has already been reached.
findings.failure_mode: With max_retries=0, or after earlier failures consume the retry allowance, a shrinkable ProviderContextLimitError changes the request but never retries it. Execution falls through to retry exhaustion instead of succeeding with the smaller budget or propagating the typed context error for calibration.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the single context-budget correction an explicit retry allowance, or propagate ProviderContextLimitError when no retry can actually occur. Do not continue past the final loop iteration.

findings.description: The pre-flight gate replaces the heuristic with the provider's count_tokens result and stores it in `_walk_estimate` (lines 1840-1841). The per-hop I1 fit (line 2090) reuses `_walk_estimate`, but the per-hop walk gate immediately below (line 2118 onward) still imports `estimate_tokens` and recomputes the chars/3.5 heuristic, comparing that against the same policy bound returned by `_lookup_max_input_tokens(..., max_tokens=_hop_budget)`. Two different input numbers are evaluated against one bound within the same hop.
findings.failure_mode: When count_tokens <= bound < heuristic (exactly the CJK / tool-payload cases D-1.4 was built for), the pre-flight warns and dispatches, then the walk gate records the head hop as ROUTING_MISS and falls to the fallback chain. The authoritative count is silently discarded at the head hop; the operator sees a dispatch on a model they never selected, and the envelope's `estimated_input_tokens` (the count) contradicts the walk-gate message (the heuristic).
findings.suggested_fix: In the walk gate use `_walk_estimate` when it is not None (it already holds the count or the heuristic) instead of calling `estimate_tokens(messages)` again; only fall back to `estimate_tokens` when `_walk_estimate` is None.

findings.description: The RateLimitError arm checks only `_ceiling_unverified`, a flag set once from the HEAD entry's pre-flight outcome (line 1843) and never recomputed per hop. Two consequences: (a) any 429 on any hop, including a plain requests-per-minute throttle, ends the invocation as RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED with a calibration record whenever the head ran above its probed bound; the error object carries no token-limit discriminator and none is consulted. (b) A fallback hop that is calibrated (or has a larger bound) inherits the head's unverified status, so its 429 is not walked and its ProviderContextLimitError (line 2256) is misclassed CEILING_UNVERIFIED_LIMIT instead of PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT. The shipped e2e tests `test_request_rate_429_while_unverified_walks_to_the_next_hop` and `test_unverified_status_is_per_hop_not_inherited_from_the_head` assert the opposite behaviour and cannot pass against this code.
findings.failure_mode: Under LOA_CHEVAL_UNCALIBRATED_CEILING=derived a transient rate-limit 429 on the head (the transport already backed off) terminates the run with exit RATE_LIMITED and writes a spurious row to `.run/ceiling-observed.json`, instead of walking to the declared fallback. The operator's chain shape is overridden by an unrelated throttle; the observed store accumulates noise rows that later surface as calibration_needed.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute unverified status per hop (the head's `_preflight_outcome.unverified` for index 0; for other hops derive it from `input_bound(entry)` vs `_walk_estimate`). Gate the short-circuit on a token-limit 429 only (add `token_limited` to RateLimitError, set by the adapter from the 429 body/headers), so a request-rate 429 keeps walking.

findings.description: The one-shot output-budget shrink does `continue`, consuming an attempt from `range(max_retries + 1)`, and does not set `last_typed_error`. If the shrinkable context error arrives on the final attempt (max_retries == 0, or after earlier 429/5xx attempts used the budget), the loop simply exits and the post-loop RetriesExhaustedError fires with either no typed error or the earlier RateLimitError.
findings.failure_mode: The provider's size verdict is downgraded to RetriesExhaustedError, so cheval's `except ProviderContextLimitError` arm never runs: no observed-bound record, no calibration_needed, and the generic exhausted handler walks the SAME oversized payload to the next hop, which D-1.1b states must never happen.
findings.suggested_fix: Set `last_typed_error = e` before `continue`, and either perform the shrunk retry outside the attempt budget (a dedicated inner retry) or `raise e` when `attempt == max_retries`.

findings.description: `_calibration_needed_exit` places the raw provider error text (`str(_exc)`) into `models_failed[].message_redacted` and into the stderr `_error_json` message. The envelope path is later redacted by the MODELINV emitter, but the stderr JSON line is not routed through any redaction, and the field name promises redaction at the point of construction. The e2e test `test_calibration_exit_redacts_secret_shapes_in_the_recorded_message` patches the emitter's redactor to identity and still expects the secret to be absent, so it would fail against this code.
findings.failure_mode: A provider 400 body that echoes request content (keys embedded in a prompt, bearer tokens in a tool result) is written verbatim to the operator's stderr log and to any pipeline capturing it.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `str(_exc)` through the existing redaction helper (the one the emitter uses) before building `_calib`, the models_failed row, and the `_error_json` message.

findings.description: The long-context tier triggers on `input_tokens > threshold`, but Anthropic's `input_tokens` excludes `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens` (the ledger's own docstring says so). The provider applies the premium on the full prompt size. A 150K-cached + 100K-fresh request is billed at base rates here while the provider bills the premium; conversely the multipliers are then applied to cache costs only when the uncached part alone exceeds the threshold.
findings.failure_mode: Systematic under-reporting of cost for cache-heavy long-context traffic, and `long_context_rows` in cost-report.sh undercounts, precisely on the workloads the 1M window is used for.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare `input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_creation_tokens` against the threshold.

findings.description: `wire_temperature` returns 0.7 under LOA_CHEVAL_LEGACY_WIRE when the caller set nothing. The old `elif request.temperature != 0.7` guard that suppressed the 'temperature dropped' log for the implicit default is gone, so every call to a `temperature_supported: false` entry under the kill switch logs a drop the caller never requested.
findings.failure_mode: Noise at the configured log level on every thinking-model call in legacy-wire deployments; operators lose the signal the cycle-124 FR-1 warning was meant to carry.
findings.suggested_fix: Log only when `request.temperature is not None` (a caller-supplied value), not when the value came from the legacy default.

findings.description: `_obs` falls back to `int(_walk_estimate or 0)` when the provider message carries no token count. With LOA_CHEVAL_DISABLE_INPUT_GATE=1 `_walk_estimate` is None, so `record_observed` is called with `observed_input_tokens=0` for a PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT row. No plausibility floor is applied before the write.
findings.failure_mode: A zero (or tiny) observation lands in `.run/ceiling-observed.json` and, per the ceiling module's 'observed - 1' bound rule, can collapse the entry's bound to 0 or -1 until an operator deletes the row, pre-empting every subsequent request on that model.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip the record (but still emit calibration_needed) when no positive observation is available, and require `observed_input_tokens >= FLOOR_MAX_TOKENS` or similar before lowering a bound.

findings.description: Only a 404 from `GET /models` falls through to the one-token message probe. Gateways and proxies that front the Messages API (LiteLLM, corporate relays, Bedrock-style shims) commonly answer unknown routes with 401, 403, 405, or 501, which now return False outright.
findings.failure_mode: A fully functional proxied Anthropic endpoint is reported unhealthy by loa-status and any health-gated chain logic, where the previous message probe would have succeeded.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat any non-200 from `/models` other than an authentication failure on a known-direct endpoint as 'not served' and fall through to the message probe; or fall through on any non-200.
